quote: 3.) Beweis des Weber'schen Satzes, dass die Idealklassenanzahl[?] des Körpers $\sqrt[2^h]{1}$ ungerade ist
english: 3.) Proof of Weber's theorem that the (ideal) class number of the field of the 2^h-th root of 1 is odd.
topic: A list of research and dissertation topics: the discriminant and invariants of the quartic, Poincaré cycles of differential equations, rotation of a body filled with fluid, three number-theoretic doctoral topics (class fields, Fermat's theorem, Weber's theorem), and independence of the laws 1-17 for complex number systems.

triage.modern_statement: Prove that for every h ≥ 1 the class number of the 2-power cyclotomic field Q(ζ_{2^h}) is odd. The classical form of the theorem, as Weber proved it, is that the class number h_n of the real subfield Q(ζ_{2^{n+2}}+ζ_{2^{n+2}}^{-1}) = Q(2cos(2π/2^{n+2})) is odd. This subfield is the n-th layer of the cyclotomic Z_2-extension of Q. Hilbert lists it as a doctoral topic, which suggests he wanted a new or simpler proof of a theorem Weber had already published.
triage.answered_by: Heinrich Weber himself proved it more than a century ago, in his 'Theorie der Abel'schen Zahlkörper' (Acta Mathematica, 1886). So the theorem was already known when Hilbert wrote this note, and the topic asked for a new proof. I did not find which student, if any, took up this dissertation topic. A related, stronger question is still open: Weber's class number problem, which asks whether h_n = 1 for all n. Fukuda, Komatsu, Morisawa, Miller and others have worked on it.

evidence.claim: Fukuda and Komatsu: let h_n be the class number of Q(2cos(2π/2^{n+2})). More than one hundred years ago, Weber [Weber 86] proved that h_n is odd for all n ≥ 1.

Weber studied the class numbers of the real cyclotomic fields Q(ζ_{2^k}+ζ_{2^k}^{-1}) and proved that they are odd for all k. The conjecture that these class numbers equal 1 is known as Weber's class number problem and is supported by the Cohen–Lenstra heuristics.
Weber proved that h_n (n ≥ 1) is odd. Horie proved that h_n is not divisible by any prime ℓ ≡ 3,5 (mod 8). Fukuda and Komatsu extended the list of excluded primes.
A 2022 survey, 'Weber's class number problem and its variants', shows the topic is still being researched.
More recent work links Weber's class number problem to p-rationality in the cyclotomic Ẑ-extension of Q.

triage.why: This oddness result is the standard 'Weber's theorem' on 2-power cyclotomic fields. Weber proved it for the real subfields in 1886, before Hilbert's note. The sources I found state the theorem for the real subfield Q(ζ_{2^h})^+, not for Q(ζ_{2^h}) itself. My view that oddness for the full field follows by the standard argument (2 is totally ramified, so h^+ divides h, and h^- is odd) is my own inference; none of the sources cited here states it. So the note asks for a proof of a known theorem, not an open problem. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems. The natural next question, whether the class number is exactly 1 (Weber's class number problem), is still open and actively studied: by computation, by Iwasawa theory, and by work ruling out small prime divisors.
